Package com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest

Class BarColumnChecks

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest.BarColumnChecks
public final class BarColumnChecks extends Object
Bar support and collapse in a live level that does not touch loader-native automation directly: item validity, grounding at the bottom of a column, footprint overlap deciding support across the alternating layer orientations, and player extraction dropping what it unsupports. Capability/Transfer-API-facing tests, and Forge's event-bus-driven protection test, stay in each loader's own BarColumnGameTests.

    • validityAndBottomGroundingAreEnforced

      public static void validityAndBottomGroundingAreEnforced(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: select Bar with V + right-click air, then V + right-click a floor with two accepted ingots. One bar is placed and one ingot remains in Survival. Offer a stick to a bottom position; it is refused without spending the stick.

    • barAdmissionFollowsTheIngotTag

      public static void barAdmissionFollowsTheIngotTag(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: select Bar and V-deposit an iron, gold, copper, and netherite ingot, a brick, and a nether brick; each becomes a bar. V-deposit a stick or an iron nugget; nothing happens. Select Singles and V-deposit an iron ingot; it is refused there too.

    • upperBarRequiresOverlappingSupport

      public static void upperBarRequiresOverlappingSupport(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: create one bottom-layer Bar with an accepted ingot. Try depositing into a second-layer position with no bar under its footprint, then into a position overlapping the bottom bar. Only the supported position accepts the ingot.

    • playerExtractionDropsUnsupportedBars

      public static void playerExtractionDropsUnsupportedBars(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: deposit one accepted ingot on the bottom layer and one overlapping bar on the next layer, with no other supports. Release V and plain-right-click the bottom bar with an empty hand. One ingot enters the hand, the unsupported upper bar drops, and the empty block disappears.

    • supportedNeighborSurvivesPlayerExtraction

      public static void supportedNeighborSurvivesPlayerExtraction(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: place two neighboring bottom bars and an upper bar overlapping the second. Plain-right-click the first bottom bar with an empty hand. The upper bar remains supported by the second bottom bar and no bar drops.

    • differentlyOrientedSeamUsesFootprintOverlap

      public static void differentlyOrientedSeamUsesFootprintOverlap(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The fixture directly fills a top-layer position of the lower block and deposits into an overlapping bottom position of the upper block.

      To check the visible seam: build a supported Bar column to its top layer, then V-deposit an accepted ingot into an overlapping position in a Bar block above it. The perpendicular layers support the new bar through footprint overlap.

    • breakingLowerBlockCollapsesDependentUpperBlock

      public static void breakingLowerBlockCollapsesDependentUpperBlock(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The fixture seeds one top-layer bar below one dependent bar in the next block.

      To check manually: build a supported two-block Bar column and break the lower block. Its contents drop and dependent bars above collapse; an emptied upper block disappears. The sparse fixture asserts two total dropped ingots.

    • breakingFullColumnConsolidatesDrops

      public static void breakingFullColumnConsolidatesDrops(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: fill two contiguous Bar blocks with 128 identical accepted ingots, then break the lower block. Both blocks disappear and all 128 ingots drop. The automated check asserts 64 ingots at each originating block, allowing the container drop helper to split stacks; later vanilla item-entity merging is outside this check.

    • breakingFullColumnDropsWithBlockDropsDisabled

      public static void breakingFullColumnDropsWithBlockDropsDisabled(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: set /gamerule doTileDrops false, fill two contiguous Bar blocks with accepted ingots, then break the lower block. All 128 ingots drop from their originating blocks and both blocks disappear. Restore the gamerule afterward.

    • playerCascadeDropsWithBlockDropsDisabled

      public static void playerCascadeDropsWithBlockDropsDisabled(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: set /gamerule doTileDrops false and build a chain of one supported bar in each layer of two Bar blocks. Extract the lowest bar with an empty hand. One ingot enters the hand, fifteen drop from their originating blocks, and both blocks disappear. Restore the gamerule afterward.

    • playerCascadeConsolidatesAcrossBlocks

      public static void playerCascadeConsolidatesAcrossBlocks(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: build a chain of one bar in each of the sixteen layers of two Bar blocks, each overlapping its sole support below. Plain-right-click the lowest bar with an empty hand. One ingot enters the hand and fifteen drop; both empty blocks disappear. The check inspects drops before vanilla merging: seven from below and eight from above.

    • collapseDoesNotMergeDifferentTags

      public static void collapseDoesNotMergeDifferentTags(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: use /give to obtain two accepted ingots with distinct custom NBT, such as {somestacks_test_variant:1} and {somestacks_test_variant:2}. Place them in the two second-layer positions supported by a single bottom bar. Extract that support with an empty hand. Both upper bars drop with their original tags and remain distinct stacks.

    • comparatorReservesZeroForAnEmptyColumn

      public static void comparatorReservesZeroForAnEmptyColumn(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The fixture checks an empty Bar block, one occupied position, then all 64 positions: signals are 0, 1, and 15.

      To reproduce the visible readings: place a comparator facing away from a Bar block, deposit one accepted ingot, then fill all positions. Read 1 and 15; after extracting all bars, the block disappears and the comparator reads 0.

    • comparatorReadsTheWholeColumnFromEveryBlock

      public static void comparatorReadsTheWholeColumnFromEveryBlock(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Internal layout check: the fixture fills all 64 positions of a lower Bar block and leaves its contiguous upper block empty. Both block signal queries return 8 for the half-full run. Empty upper blocks are temporary, so there is no stable manual reproduction of that exact layout.

      For the visible behavior, build two contiguous partly filled Bar blocks and put an outward-facing comparator beside each on a solid support. Both report the same whole-run fill after updates.

    • comparatorFollowsAColumnLosingABlock

      public static void comparatorFollowsAColumnLosingABlock(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Internal layout check: a full lower Bar block and empty upper block report 8; removing the upper block changes the lower signal to 15.

      To check the visible capacity change, fill a lower Bar block and add one bar in a supported block above. The comparator reads 8. Extract the upper bar; its empty block disappears and the full remaining block reads 15.
